subject: Kickoff: dual-pixel depth for the imaging pipeline
body:
Hi all,

Kicking off the dual-pixel depth effort. Our open-source release showed you can learn single-camera depth estimation from dual-pixel data — the DPNet model with affine invariance is the reference — and the released dataset (95G train, 29G test, with RGB, dual-pixel images, and depth maps) is big enough to train production-grade models.

Product target: depth-driven features in the on-device imaging pipeline — portrait relighting and defocus effects — without any additional hardware, since dual-pixel sensors are already in the camera stack.

Milestones: reproduce the paper's metrics on the released test split by end of April, mobile-feasible model by end of May, integration decision with the imaging platform team at the June 15 review.

The affine-invariant eval matters here: depth up to affine transform is fine for defocus, trickier for relighting — Fumiko, let's dig into that early.

Bruno owns staffing/compute.

Lucia
